name: Bizarreness Effect
description: Unusual, bizarre, or incongruous material can be remembered better than ordinary material, especially when its distinctiveness stands out against a more normal surrounding context. The memorability comes from relative distinctiveness, not from 'weirdness' as a universal design virtue.
design_relevance_note: Occasionally relevant to campaigns, onboarding moments, educational content, and standout reminders, but it is a weak basis for making core interface patterns weird for their own sake. If used at all, it argues for targeted distinctiveness, not blanket novelty.
prevalence_note: Mostly a memory-psychology and mnemonic-design concept, occasionally borrowed into advertising or learning design, but rarely named in mainstream digital-product UX practice.

findings.description: Bizarre imagery improved memory as a mnemonic aid when it was relatively distinctive, supporting the bizarreness effect while tying its benefit specifically to distinctiveness rather than to weirdness in the abstract.
findings.source_title: Bizarre imagery as an effective memory aid: The importance of distinctiveness.
findings.source_venue: Journal of Experimental Psychology: Learning, Memory, and Cognition
